So it's important to maintain harmony, as evidenced in the cave paintings from the dawn of humanity. We believe animals came from the spirit world and were painted to thank them for nourishing us; after they were killed, prayers ensured their return. This belief spans tens of thousands of years.

In Africa, among the pygmies who live in the forest, ritual participation is crucial. If you refuse or break these rituals, you risk ostracization or death. Colin Turbo wrote about a religious festival where all adult males had to sing during Malomo singing; sleeping was considered a severe crime. Disrespecting rituals meant forgetting and possibly killing.

When something goes wrong at night, army ants invade camps, leopards steal hunting dogs or children. If awake, these would be prevented. Illness, bad hunts, or deaths are seen as forest sleep. Waking it up by singing restores balance and harmony, ensuring a good world. Their idea of God is heaven on earth where environment impacts everything and practices maintain this balance.

Nowadays, people lack vision and imagination compared to ancient times, yet we can build skyscrapers. The question is: why can't we rebuild pyramids?
